summary.headline: Triton Valves Q1 FY27 group consolidated sales rose 38.5% YoY to ₹186.5 crore; EBITDA ₹12.4 crore, with ₹4.75 crore one-time tax credit lifting PAT to ~₹9.75 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported group consolidated sales of about ₹186.5 crore, up roughly 17.5% QoQ and 38.5% YoY, with about 20% volume growth and the rest value growth. EBITDA was about ₹12.4 crore versus ₹11.3 crore QoQ and ₹8.8 crore YoY (the slide labelled the YoY figure incorrectly). Gross margin contracted about 145 bps QoQ and 181 bps YoY, which management attributed to commodity pass-through with copper and brass prices near historic highs and the Iran/war disruption. Management also flagged that climate control shrank, metals was hit by delayed Middle East raw material supply, and the merger tax credit flattered PAT.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Sales ₹103 crore, up from ₹78 crore YoY and ₹86 crore QoQ; growth led by tubeless (~25% volume YoY), TPMS (~75-80% YoY) and EV components (~103% YoY). Tube valves ex-motorcycle segment grew ~20%. Tubeless, TPMS and EV lines running above 85-90% utilisation.

segments.name: Metals (Triton Valves Future Tech, brass mill)
segments.commentary: Sales ~₹79 crore, up from ~₹50-52 crore YoY and ₹68 crore QoQ; capacity utilisation ~65-70% post expansion, implying ~30% headroom. Current ROCE above 16%, with management targeting 20%+ and possibly 25%. Scrap sales now netted off under Ind AS, reducing reported standalone top line without affecting EBITDA.

segments.name: Climate control
segments.commentary: Sales ~₹3.9 crore, down YoY and QoQ. Management cited Chinese dumping, copper costs and a weak AC season; it is lobbying for QCO and minimum import price. Q2 expected to be quiet, with recovery from Oct-Nov.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of a 'reasonably good' Q2 if the second half of the quarter holds, and says FY27 will be much better than FY26.
Annualised Q1 group EBITDA ~₹50 crore vs ~₹40 crore in FY26; PBT, EBITDA and revenue expected to run slightly above annualised Q1 levels.
Group ROCE expected to rise from ~12.5% to 13-14% this year and ~15% by mid-next year; new investments targeted at 20-25% internal ROCE.
Ambition of a ₹1,000 crore revenue target by about FY30; management says it has a plan that does not depend on climate control recovery.
EV component vertical targeted at ~₹100 crore over the next few quarters, with climate control also scaling to ~₹100 crore if trade remediation happens.
Double-digit EBITDA margin is not expected until commodity prices stabilise; management said it would take a long time.
Tax credit of ~₹4.75 crore already availed, plus a further ~₹0.3-0.4 crore claimed, subject to assessment; no advance tax outflow expected for ~14-15 months.
capex_capacity: FY27 group capex planned at ~₹15 crore: ~₹10 crore for automotive (tubeless, TPMS, EV components) and ~₹5 crore for metals (special alloy foundry, extrusion and drawing equipment).
About 50-60% of the ₹15 crore is expected to be commercialised in FY27, with the balance in FY28.
Automotive tubeless, TPMS and EV lines are at 85-90%+ utilisation; management said capacity will run out during the year without investment.
Metals utilisation ~65-70% post expansion, leaving ~30% volume headroom.
Climate control has spare capacity; management said it only needs orders.
demand_pricing: Automotive growth described as ~80% vehicle production growth and ~20% share gain; passenger car and two-wheeler production grew ~12-15% YoY in Q1 (per management).
Management expects automotive growth to moderate in Q3-Q4 but remain positive; new programmes cited with AUMOVIO, SENSATA and Bosch (LOIs from AUMOVIO and SENSATA in TPMS).

Metals: Q1 started slowly from Middle East raw material disruption; ~₹10 crore of metals sales were not delivered on time due to Hormuz issues. Demand strong into Q2; management expects Q3 seasonal traction in metals and climate control.
Prices pass through to automotive and climate control customers every three months. Brass selling price to external customers now above ₹1,000/kg vs ~₹500-550/kg last July-August.
Management expects metals to reach 60%+ of group revenue over 2-3 years; special alloys (naval brass, marine grades) being developed as import substitutes.
Climate control faces Chinese dumping; management is refusing to cut margins to win volume.
